claims.summary: Observed: scan_known_model_control_markers (L114) is non-destructive; only markers with a reference_syntax (quoted/grouped/relation verb such as 'appears'/'denotes') are kept in the remainder, others stripped, non-marker bytes copied.
claims.disposition: verified_existing. Complete source: scan_known_model_control_markers L114-144 pushes the marker into remainder only when reference_syntax.is_some() (L129-131); reference_syntax L49-60 = delimiter syntax OR followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation; 'appears' L67, 'denotes' L71 are allowlisted; non-marker chars copied byte-exact L133-140.

claims.summary: Likely Snag: first_word_after (L89) split_whitespace + trim_matches(!alnum && !'_') might strip punctuation significant to the model's tokenization, causing a mismatch between reference detection and the following word's actual tokenization.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; concern preserved, mechanism contradicted. first_word_after L89-96 runs on already-generated output during cleanup, not on tokenization, so no reference-vs-tokenization mismatch is possible. split_whitespace absorbs newlines/multiple spaces; trim only strips leading/trailing non-alnum. Committed L2873 (newline), L2884 (multi-punct), L2635, L2987, L3029 already ground the whitespace/punctuation boundary.

claims.summary: Test 1 (Reference Preservation): '[MARKER] denotes X' should keep the marker in remainder because followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64) returns true.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; located precisely. For a BRACKETED marker, preservation fires first via the grouped delimiter path (exact_reference_delimiter_syntax L50), not the relation path; the relation path applies to a BARE marker. Both are covered: scan_known_model_control_markers_preserves_grouped_and_explicit_relation_contexts (tests.rs L2932, bare '<end_of_turn> behaves as...'); 'denotes' allowlisted L71. '[MARKER]' is a placeholder, not a real marker.

claims.summary: Test 2 (Delimiter Depth): '[[MARKER]]' should be classified GroupedExactKnownToken by exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) respecting MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH (L151=4).
claims.disposition: verified_existing. exact_reference_delimiter_syntax L199-229 collects <=4 non-whitespace chars each side; '[[<end_of_turn>]]' => GroupedExactKnownToken, depth 2. Covered verbatim by exact_reference_delimiter_syntax_reports_double_square_bracket_depth_two (tests.rs L2963); depth-3/4 and beyond-max at L2194/L2208/L2266.

claims.summary: Suggested Next: verify scan_known_model_control_markers when a marker is at the very end of a string (no 'after' text) — ensure it does not panic or strip incorrectly.
claims.disposition: implemented_now. Traced complete source: empty tail => first_word_after returns empty (L89-96), exact_reference_delimiter_syntax gets an empty after-window => None (L210-215), so reference_syntax=None and the bare end-of-string marker is stripped byte-exactly; the L137 expect is never reached (marker branch taken). Existing coverage exercised this only incidentally ('hello <end_of_turn>' in a diagnostic test L1821). Added a dedicated regression at the exact cited functions.
